question: Which party will win the most votes in Spain's November 29, 2026 general election?

calls.reasoning: Private polls 22 Oct-1 Nov show PP leading PSOE by 1-7 pp (most 4-7, roughly 5 on average); only CIS and partisan polls (The Objective, PSOE internal) have PSOE ahead. Base rate: in Spanish elections a ~5pp poll leader four weeks out usually wins the popular vote, but 2023 polls overstated PP's lead by ~3-5pp and PSOE is gaining slightly now. Taking a lead of about 5 shaded for the 2023 miss, with total uncertainty of about 4pp, gives PSOE roughly a 16-19% chance. Polymarket has PP at 85.5% for most SEATS and Feijóo at 84% for PM; neither is a most-votes contract, and PP's rural seat bonus means most votes should sit a little below most seats. Vox is ~6-7pp behind PSOE and needs a large break to come first.
calls.dossier:
- Election to the Congress of Deputies on 29 Nov 2026; resolves on most valid votes nationwide (JEC/Interior results), NOT on most seats. PSOE includes PSC; PP includes coalitions it leads (e.g. PP-Foro).
- Event window: the vote on 29 Nov 2026 -> proclaimed results; as of 2026-11-03, 26 days before the vote.
- Wikipedia polling tracker (accessed 2026-11-03), PP/PSOE/Vox/FA: SocioMétrica 1 Sep-1 Nov 32.7/26.6/19.1/5.2; Sigma Dos 29-30 Oct 31.1/24.6/19.3/7.5; Target Point 28-30 Oct 31.8/25.5/19.9/6.6; EM-Analytics 28-30 Oct 31.5/25.8/19.2/6.2; NC Report 26-29 Oct 33.0/25.6/19.3/6.9; Sondaxe 26-28 Oct 29.2/26.9/19.2/7.2; Hamalgama 22-28 Oct 32.4/26.4/19.9/5.4; Winston 21-23 Oct 29.4/27.1/19.2/5.6; Ateneo del Dato/elDiario.es 20-22 Oct 31.1/27.6/19.8/6.8.
- PSOE ahead only in: The Objective 27 Oct (PSOE 29.6, PP 28.1), a PSOE internal poll 25 Oct (30 vs 29), and CIS 14 Oct (PSOE 34.0, PP 22.2; CIS is government-run and has historically leaned PSOE).
- DatosRTVE average as of 23 Oct: PP 31.5, PSOE 26.8, Vox 18.7, FA 6.9.
- Infobae 27 Oct: slight PP decline, modest PSOE recovery in 2 of 3 polls, Vox stable or rising.
- Since 1982 every popular-vote winner has been PP or PSOE (14 of 14 elections).
- 2023: final polls showed PP leading PSOE by about 4-7pp; the result was PP 33.1 vs PSOE 31.7 (+1.4), so polls overstated PP's lead by about 3-5pp. 2019 polls were closer.
- Vox has never polled above about 20% or finished above third; its 2019 peak was 15.1%.
- Prediction markets (Polymarket) exist only for most seats and next PM, not most votes. PP's rural-province seat bonus means most-seats and most-votes can diverge.
- Searched but not found: a most-votes market on Kalshi or with bookmakers; a reason/context for why the election was called for 29 Nov.
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 1982-2023: popular-vote winner vs the poll-average leader about 1 month before the vote, adjusted for historical final-poll error on the PP-PSOE lead

calls.reasoning: Base rate: since 1982 only PP or PSOE have topped the vote; when one leads polling averages by ~5 pts a month out, it usually wins. Private-poll average ~PP 31.4 vs PSOE 26.3 (Colmena, Nov wk1); Sondaxe narrowest +2.3, Sigma Dos +6.5; CIS outlier gives PSOE +11.8. Spanish poll lead errors ~3-4 pts SD (2023 overstated PP lead ~3), giving PSOE ~10-15%. Markets: no most-votes market found; Polymarket most-seats PP 85.5c / Kalshi 82c (Nov 3) — near-miss contract (seats vs votes), and votes are slightly less PP-favourable than seats. Vox at ~19% is ~12 pts behind; negligible. Post-Urda train crash effects unmeasured.
calls.dossier:
- Election to Congress of Deputies on Sunday 29 Nov 2026, called by Sánchez on 5 Oct (Rio Times). Sánchez-Feijóo debate is scheduled for 16 Nov.
- DatosRTVE average, 23 Oct: PP 31.5, PSOE 26.8, Vox 18.7, Frente Amplio 6.9 (question background).
- Colmena de Datos average, Nov week 1: PP 31.4 (-1.2 vs prior month), PSOE 26.3 (+0.6).
- Sondaxe, published 1 Nov, fieldwork 26-28 Oct (before the Urda train crash): PP 29.2, PSOE 26.9, Vox 19.2, FA 7.2, Podemos 2.0 (Rio Times / Infobae 3 Nov).
- Sigma Dos, 2 Nov: PP 31.1 (133-139 seats), PSOE 24.6 (97-103), Vox ~19; PSOE -1.5 week-over-week (Rio Times).
- SocioMétrica (El Español), late Oct: PP 32% / 135 seats, PSOE 27% / 108, Vox 63 seats. Sigma Dos 26 Oct: PP 125-131, PSOE 103-109. Hamalgama Oct: PP 144, PSOE 103 (Infobae 27 Oct).
- CIS, 14 Oct: PSOE 34.0 vs PP 22.2. CIS has a history of pro-PSOE house effects.
- A claimed internal Vox poll putting PSOE ahead was denied by Vox (democrata.es).
- Urda (Toledo) train collision on 28 Oct; post-crash polling impact is not yet clear.

- Prediction markets exist for most seats and next PM, not most votes. A near-miss contract: seats favour the leading party, and votes can diverge from seats when the race is close.
- Status quo: PP leads every private poll.
- Resolves off the proclaimed nationwide valid votes for Congress (JEC / Interior Ministry), not seats. PSOE includes PSC; PP includes PP-led coalitions (e.g. PP-Foro).
- Event window: votes cast 29 Nov 2026; as of 3 Nov, 26 days remain before election day.
- Searched but not found: a most-votes market, and post-crash polls besides Sigma Dos.
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections since 1982 where one major party led the polling average by ~4-6 points about one month before the vote

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Spanish general elections since 1982. PP or PSOE topped the vote in all 14, and the poll leader about four weeks out won the vote in most of them. The current independent-poll average is about PP 31.5–32 / PSOE 26–26.5 / Vox 19, a lead of about 5.5 points. That lead is narrowing slightly, with PSOE gaining in some polls. 2023 is the cautionary precedent: final polls showed a lead of about 6 points and the real margin was 1.4. So a polling miss of about 4–5 points on the lead is plausible, and PSOE does need one of roughly that size. Polls showing PSOE ahead are outliers: CIS (PSOE 34–22, with a known pro-PSOE house effect), The Objective on 27 Oct (PSOE 29.6–28.1) and a PSOE internal poll. Polymarket's 'Spain General Election Winner' market has PP at about 87¢ and PSOE about 12¢ on $290k volume. Its contract is probably about seats rather than votes; seats favour PP slightly more because of rural overrepresentation, so I shade PSOE up a little for votes. Vox, at about 19%, would need an unprecedented 12-point move.

calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections since 1982 (14 elections): the party leading national polls about four weeks out, by a mid-single-digit margin, compared with the actual vote-share winner

calls.reasoning: PP or PSOE has topped the national vote in all 14 Spanish elections since 1982. Private polls from late October put PP ahead of PSOE by about 5-5.5 points (range +2.3 to +7.4), 26 days before the vote. The trend is mixed: Infobae and Colmena show PSOE edging up, while Sigma Dos shows PSOE down 1.5 points. In 2023 the polls overstated PP's lead over PSOE by about 4-5 points, which keeps PSOE's chance well above negligible. A lead error with an SD of about 4 points gives PSOE roughly 15-18%. The most-seats markets (Polymarket 85.5-87%, Kalshi about 82% for PP) are near-miss contracts that favour PP slightly over a most-votes question. Vox, about 7 points behind PSOE and about 12 behind PP, would need an unprecedented shift to finish first.
calls.reconciliation: The runs differed on PSOE only between 14.5% and 18.2%, and on the same evidence. Factual points: (1) Polymarket's most-seats price was reported as 85.5 or 87 cents. That gap is timing or snapshot noise and doesn't matter, and every run agreed the contract is about seats, not votes, so it is a near-miss. (2) Run 2's Kalshi price of 82 cents for most seats could not be checked, but it agrees with the others. (3) The direction of the poll trend is mixed: Infobae and Colmena show PSOE edging up, and Sigma Dos after the crash shows PSOE down 1.5 points. I treated this as no clear trend. Judgment: how much the 2023 PP overstatement should carry over. I gave it moderate weight because Spanish polls have overstated PP before but not systematically every time, and a 26-day horizon adds campaign variance. That puts PSOE at about 17%. I rejected the CIS outlier because of its known pro-PSOE house effect.

disagreements.verdict: Snapshot timing difference. Immaterial, and the contract is a near-miss (seats), so it is evidence only.

disagreements.claim: Whether PSOE is gaining (Infobae/Colmena) or slipping (Sigma Dos post-crash)
disagreements.verdict: Couldn't be settled without new polls. Treated as no clear trend.

disagreements.claim: How much to discount PP's lead for the 2023-style polling miss
disagreements.verdict: Moderate discount. Effective lead about 4-5 points with SD about 4, so PSOE about 17%.

disagreements.claim: How far the most-votes chance should sit below the most-seats market price
disagreements.verdict: A few points below, because rural seat overrepresentation favours PP.
